narrative:

The strongest factor was your Law School Admission Test score. At 24, it is far below the average of 37.18 among accepted students, and it pushed the prediction most strongly toward failure. The second strongest factor was your third-year class standing: a decile of 3 compared with an accepted-student average of 5.79, and this position contributed toward the failure estimate. The third factor was your undergraduate GPA of 2.40, below the accepted-student average of 3.23, adding further weight toward the failure prediction. Your gender and race were not used in the prediction.

To respond, request admissions feedback and ask what evidence would address these concerns. Consider intensive test preparation and a retake, and strengthen your academic record through additional coursework or a structured post-baccalaureate program. Meet with an advisor to discuss extenuating circumstances and a realistic reapplication plan. The prediction is a risk estimate, not a final judgment, so focus on demonstrating improved readiness.
